codex_review.sh
---
name: review-loop
description: Run a set of review lenses (slop and simplify, correctness and security, naming on a PR that changes a contract, or simplify and naming on a design) in rounds until every lens rates Low or three rounds pass, hand the findings to the owner, keep a context file of settled decisions between rounds, and record the result on the PR or, for a design, in the spec folder. Picks the model for each lens. Reuses an earlier record instead of reviewing again. Use when an implementing agent finishes a non-obvious PR, when the build workflow reaches a review gate, when the release merge queue lands an external or quick PR with no record, when a spec needs its design review, or when asked to "run the review loop", "loop simplify and slop on this PR", "run the Codex correctness and security review", "review this spec for simplicity", "review the naming of this PR", or "has this PR been reviewed".
---

# Review loop

You run one lens set on one target, round by round, and record the result. You do not write
code or edit the spec yourself unless the caller tells you to. The owner fixes the findings.

## Lens sets and models

The caller names one lens set. The model for each lens is fixed here, not in the lens skills.

| Lens set | Target | Lenses | Models |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `slop-simplify` (default) | PR diff | `review-slop`, `review-simplify` | Round 1: Opus and Codex on each lens. Rounds 2 and 3: one model per lens, alternating. |
| `correctness-security` | PR diff | `review-correctness`, `review-security` | Codex only, every round. |
| `naming` | PR diff that changes a contract (table, column, index, route, DTO field, enum value, config field, UI label) | `review-naming` | Round 1: Opus and Codex. Rounds 2 and 3: one model, alternating (Codex, then Opus). |
| `design` | Spec folder or architecture doc | `review-simplify`, `review-naming` (design target) | Simplify: Codex only, every round. Naming: round 1 Opus and Codex, rounds 2 and 3 alternating (Codex, then Opus). |

Codex always runs `gpt-6-astra` at effort `medium`, through `scripts/codex_review.sh`. Opus
runs as a subagent with `model: opus`.

## Inputs

- **Lens set.** One of the four above. Run `naming` next to `slop-simplify` when the PR
  changes a contract.
- **Target.** For a PR set: a PR number, or a branch and its base branch. For `design`: the
  spec folder (`openspec/changes/<name>/`) or the doc, and the repo commit it applies to
  (default: the tip of the release branch or `main`).
- **Run dir.** The caller names it, for example `~/agenta-release-0126/review/7843`. Keep every
  report, findings list, and the context file there. Never use `/tmp`.
- **Owner.** Who fixes the findings: the caller itself, or a named agent to message.
- **Mode.** `full` (default) or `quick`. A quick review gets one round.
- Optional: product rules from the owner that reviewers must not argue with. Put them at the
  top of the context file.

## Step 1: Check for an earlier record

Each lens set has its own record. A record for one set never counts for another set.

| Lens set | Record | Marker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slop-simplify` | PR comment | `<!-- review-loop: head=<sha> lenses=simplify,slop -->` |
| `correctness-security` | PR comment | `<!-- review-loop: head=<sha> lenses=correctness,security -->` |
| `naming` | PR comment | `<!-- review-loop: head=<sha> lenses=naming -->` |
| `design` | `<spec folder>/review-loop.md` | `<!-- review-loop: design=<hash> lenses=simplify,naming -->` |

For a PR set:

```bash
gh pr view <N> --json headRefOid,baseRefName,isCrossRepository,title
gh api repos/Agenta-AI/agenta/issues/<N>/comments --paginate \
  --jq '.[] | select(.body | contains("<!-- review-loop:")) | select(.body | contains("lenses=<lenses>")) | {created_at, body}'
```

Take the newest matching comment and read its `head=<sha>`.

- **Same head as now:** stop. Report the recorded result to the caller. Do not review again.
- **Head changed by a small delta:** review only the delta. Use base = the recorded head. A
  small delta means the recorded head is an ancestor of the new head
  (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <recorded> <head>`) and `git diff --shortstat <recorded> <head>`
  shows at most 400 changed lines. Run one round, then record.
- **Otherwise, or no record:** run the full loop.

For the full loop, base = `git merge-base <head> origin/<baseRefName>`. Never review against
the current tip of the base branch.

For `design`, compute the design hash:

```bash
find <spec> -type f -name '*.md' ! -name review-loop.md | sort | xargs sha256sum | sha256sum | cut -c1-12
```

If `<spec>/review-loop.md` has the same hash, stop and report it. If the hash changed, run
one round with the old context file. If there is no record, run the full loop.

## Step 2: Prepare checkouts

Use one plain clone under `/data/mahmoud/`, for example `/data/mahmoud/review-<N>` or
`/data/mahmoud/review-<spec name>`. Never use the GitButler workspace `~/code/agenta` or any
lane in it.

```bash
C=/data/mahmoud/review-<N>
[ -d $C/.git ] || git clone -q --filter=blob:none --no-checkout https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta.git $C
git -C $C fetch -q origin <head> <base> || git -C $C fetch -q origin pull/<N>/head
```

Every review runs in its own worktree. Two reviews in one folder collide on the git index
lock. The Codex script makes and removes its own worktree. For an Opus review, make one:

```bash
git -C $C worktree add -q --detach $C.wt/<round>-claude-<lens> <head>
```

## Step 3: Run a round

Start every review of the round at the same time.

**Codex**, one background call per lens:

```bash
REVIEW_PR=<N> ~/.claude/skills/review-loop/scripts/codex_review.sh \
  $C <run-dir> r1 <lens> <base> <head> [<run-dir>/context.md]
```

For `design`, set `REVIEW_DESIGN=<spec folder or doc>`, run lens `simplify` and lens `naming`,
pass `design` as the base, and pass the repo commit the design applies to as the head. The
script puts the design files into the brief, so the spec does not need to be committed.

The script feeds the brief to `codex exec` on stdin, so it never waits on a terminal. It uses
a read-only sandbox and writes `<run-dir>/r1-codex-<lens>.md` plus a `.log`. Never `pkill` by
pattern. To stop a run, kill its own PID only.

**Opus** (`slop-simplify`, `naming`, and the naming lens of `design`), one subagent per lens
with `model: opus`. Tell it: load the `review-<lens>` skill; checkout path, base, head (for a
design: the design path and the repo commit), and context file; write the report to
`<run-dir>/r1-claude-<lens>.md`; do not spawn agents.

Rounds for `slop-simplify`: round 1 runs four reviews, each lens with Opus and with Codex.
Round 2 runs Codex on simplify and Opus on slop. Round 3 swaps them.

Rounds for `naming`, and for the naming lens of `design`: round 1 runs Opus and Codex. Round 2
runs Codex. Round 3 runs Opus.

Rounds for `correctness-security`, and for the simplify lens of `design`: every round runs
each lens once with Codex.

Keep base the same as round 1, so each round sees the whole change, and the context file says
what is settled. Write the head and base of each round to `<run-dir>/rN.shas`. Remove Opus
worktrees when the round ends.

## Step 4: Merge findings and hand them to the owner

Read each report. Take the `Rating:` line from each one. Write `<run-dir>/rN-findings.md`:
one numbered list, duplicates merged, each item with its location, what is wrong, the
smallest fix, severity, and which reviewers raised it. Drop items the context file already
settles, unless a reviewer shows the fix is wrong.

Give the list to the owner. Ask for an answer per item: fixed (with the commit, or for a
design, the changed spec file), rejected (with the reason), or deferred (with where it is
tracked). For a PR, wait for the push. For a design, wait for the spec update.

## Step 5: Update the context file

Append to `<run-dir>/context.md` after each round:

```markdown
## After round N (head <sha or design hash>)
- Fixed: <item>, in <commit or spec file>.
- Rejected: <item>. Reason: <reason>.
- Deferred: <item>. Tracked in <issue or note>.

Round N+1: check that the fixes above are correct and complete, and look for new problems
the fixes added. Do not raise a rejected or deferred item again unless you show the reason
is wrong.
```

## Step 6: Stop rule

Stop when every rating in the latest round is Low. Also stop after round 3, or after round 1
in quick mode or for a delta review. If anything is above Low at the stop, list what is left
and why in the record.

## Step 7: Record the result

Load the `plain-writing` skill before you write the record.

For a PR set, post one comment. It is a public repo: no customer data, no host names or IPs,
no secrets, no local paths.

```markdown
🤖 _The AI agent says:_
<!-- review-loop: head=<head sha> lenses=<lenses> -->

**Review loop result** for head `<head sha>` (base `<base sha>`), <R> rounds.

| Lens | Final rating |
| --- | --- |
| <Lens> | Low |
| <Lens> | Low |

**Fixed:** <one line per fixed item>
**Left on purpose:** <one line per rejected or deferred item, with the reason>
```

Post with `gh pr comment <N> --body-file <run-dir>/record.md`. Post a new comment each time;
the newest marker wins.

For `design`, write the same body without the first line to `<spec folder>/review-loop.md`,
with the marker `<!-- review-loop: design=<hash> lenses=simplify,naming -->` and the repo commit in
place of the head. Compute the hash after the last spec change. Overwrite the file each time.

## Step 8: Clean up and report

Remove the worktrees and the clone. Disk space runs out on this box.

```bash
git -C $C worktree prune; rm -rf $C.wt $C
```

Report to the caller: the lens set, the reviewed head or design hash, rounds, final ratings,
the comment URL or the record path, and what is left.

## Speed

- Check for a record first. A record for the current head or design hash ends the loop.
- Start every review of a round at once: all Codex calls in the background and all Opus
  subagents in the same message. Do not wait for one lens to start the next.
- When the caller needs both PR sets, run `slop-simplify` and `correctness-security` at the
  same time in separate run dirs. They share the clone, and each review has its own worktree.
- Hand findings to the owner as soon as the round's reports are in. Do not wait for CI.
- Use the delta review for small pushes after a record, and quick mode for quick or external
  PRs.
- Wait on background runs with their completion notice, not with a polling loop.

content.content:
## Why

An event automation runs an agent when something happens in a connected app, for example
"when a pull request is opened in GitHub, review it". Today the agent gets only the
instruction text the user typed. It does not get the pull request, the email or the Slack
message that started the run, so it cannot do the job.

The cause is in two places:

- The `/m` Instruction field stores static text only. It has no way to refer to the event
  (`web/packages/agenta-entities/src/gatewayTrigger/core/messageInputs.ts:100-118`). The old
  form with an event field picker was deleted in commit `89c2d80c39`.
- The dispatcher sends only what the mapping names
  (`api/oss/src/tasks/asyncio/triggers/dispatcher.py:316-319`). The workaround that builder
  agents are told to use, a sibling `event` input key, is never read by the agent handler
  (`sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/handler.py:479`).

## What Changes

- A new subscription option `data.include_event`, on by default and on for every existing
  automation. When it is on, the dispatcher adds the event data to the agent's message. Old
  automations start to work without an edit.
- The dispatcher turns every resolved message text into a string. Without this, a field that
  is a number, an object or absent would fail the run.
- Each subscription delivery records the event it received in `data.event`, so the screen can
  show real values.
- Test-mode captures use the same message as a real run.
- The agent-facing reference text stops telling builder agents to use a sibling `event` key.
- On `/m`, for event automations only, the Instruction field gets:
  - a grid of field cards built from the event's payload schema, with a humanized name and the
    provider's own description, and a check on the cards already used;
  - pills: a click on a card inserts the field into the instruction;
  - a checkbox "Also attach the full event, so the agent can use any detail", on by default;
  - a "What the agent gets" preview, filled from the last delivery when one exists.
- "Run now" fills the pills from the last delivery and adds the event when the option is on.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `trigger-event-inputs`: how the dispatcher builds the agent's inputs for an event
  automation, including the attached event, text coercion and the recorded event.
- `automation-event-fields`: the `/m` Instruction field for event automations: field cards,
  pills, the attach option, the preview and Run now.

### Modified Capabilities

None. No spec in `openspec/specs/` covers triggers or automations yet.

## Impact

- API: `api/oss/src/core/triggers/dtos.py`, `api/oss/src/tasks/asyncio/triggers/dispatcher.py`,
  `api/oss/src/core/triggers/utils.py`, unit tests in `api/oss/tests/pytest/unit/triggers/`.
- SDK: the reference text in `sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/adapters/agenta_builtins.py`.
- Web: `@agenta/entities/gatewayTrigger` (types and pure helpers),
  `@agenta/entity-ui/gatewayTrigger` (pill composer, field cards),
  `@agenta/automation-ui` (Instruction field, drafts, payload builders), `web/mobile` (Run now).
- Generated client: two Fern type files, regenerated from an EE spec.
- Data: no migration. `data` is a JSON column on both tables. Old rows read the defaults.
- Behavior change for old automations: their agents start to get the event text in the
  message. This is the point of the change.
## Context

Terms:

- **Subscription**: the backend row behind an event automation (`TriggerSubscription`).
- **Mapping**: `data.inputs_fields`, a JSON template. The dispatcher resolves it against the
  event context and sends the result as the agent's inputs.
- **Selector**: a mapping leaf that starts with `$` (JSON Path) or `/` (JSON Pointer).
- **Event context**: `{event:{event_id,event_type,timestamp,created_at,attributes}, subscription, scope}`.
  `event.attributes` is the provider's event payload.
- **Delivery**: one row per event that reached a subscription. It records the inputs sent.
- **Pill**: a chip in the instruction text that stands for one event field, stored as a selector.
- **Payload schema**: the JSON Schema of the event payload that the provider publishes. The
  catalog route returns it as `payload`.

Today, with evidence (full notes in the research file of this build):

| Area | Today | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Instruction field | Plain text area. Writes `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<text>"}]}`. No selectors. | `web/packages/agenta-automation-ui/src/AutomationInstructionField.tsx:94-101`, `web/packages/agenta-entities/src/gatewayTrigger/core/messageInputs.ts:100-118` |
| Template helpers | `compileMessageTemplate`, `parseMessageTemplate` exist, tested, no caller. | `web/packages/agenta-entities/src/gatewayTrigger/core/eventMessageTemplate.ts:66-139` |
| Context | `attributes` is the Composio payload. | `api/oss/src/tasks/asyncio/triggers/dispatcher.py:93-118` |
| Inputs | Only what the mapping names. | `dispatcher.py:316-319`, `sdks/python/agenta/sdk/utils/resolvers.py:139-171` |
| Agent reads | Only `inputs.messages`. | `sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/handler.py:479` |
| Text parts | `ContentBlock.text` is `Optional[str]`; an int or dict fails validation. | `sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/dtos.py:394, 443-447` |
| Runner | Joins text blocks with no separator. | `services/runner/src/protocol.ts:1066-1075` |
| Storage | `data` is one JSON column, dumped with `exclude_none=True`. | `api/oss/src/dbs/postgres/shared/dbas.py:214-220`, `api/oss/src/dbs/postgres/triggers/mappings.py:55, 82, 111` |
| Delivery | Stores resolved `inputs`, not the raw event. | `api/oss/src/core/triggers/dtos.py:380-397` |
| Catalog | `GET .../integrations/{integration_key}/events/{event_key}` returns `payload`. A frontend query for it exists. | `api/oss/src/apis/fastapi/triggers/router.py:217-223, 943-995`, `web/packages/agenta-entities/src/gatewayTrigger/hooks/useTriggerEvent.ts:12-42` |
| Run now | Sends the joined instruction text in a new chat. | `web/mobile/src/features/automations/AutomationTestRunButton.tsx:39-42, 59` |

How the frontend parts map to backend ideas, for the reader who knows Python:

- `@agenta/entities` is like the `core` layer: types (zod schemas, like Pydantic models) and
  pure functions. It has unit tests with vitest, like pytest.
- `@agenta/entity-ui` is a library of reusable UI components, like a shared template library.
- `@agenta/automation-ui` is the automation feature: the screens' parts and their state.
- A React component is a function from props to UI. A hook (`useX`) is a function a component
  calls to read state or start a query; think of it as a dependency the framework injects.
- A "draft" is the unsaved form state held in memory until Save. It is like a request body
  object that the screen builds up field by field.

## Goals / Non-Goals

Goals:

- The agent of every event automation gets the event data, with no edit by the user.
- On `/m`, a user can put named event fields into the instruction without writing selectors.
- The user can see what the agent will get, with real values when a delivery exists.

Non-Goals:

- Schedules. A schedule has no event payload worth showing.
- The classic app under `/w` (playground trigger section, `RunSubscriptionButton`).
- A raw JSON editor for the mapping.
- An escape syntax for typed text that starts with `$` or `/` (a known limit, see Risks).
- Adding `include_event` to the builder agent's `create_subscription` tool schema. Agents get
  the default.
- Field cards from delivered keys. Cards come from the schema only.

## Decisions

### 1. Name and place of the option

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **`data.include_event: bool = True`** | Sits next to `inputs_fields`, which it changes. `include_` is the repo's word for "add this to the result" (`include_archived`). Needs no migration. Breaks the "booleans are `is_<adjective>`" rule, which the repo applies to state in `flags`. This is config, not state. |
| `data.attach_event` | Same place. "Attach" already means file attachments in chat (`ContentBlock` type `attachment`, `dtos.py:393`). One word would have two meanings. |
| `flags.is_event_included` | Follows the `flags` naming rule. But `flags` holds run state (`is_active`, `is_valid`, `is_test`), set by the user switch or by the system. This option is how the inputs are built. A reader looking for mapping config looks in `data`. |
| `data.event: {include: true}` | Room for more options later. No second option is planned, so the nesting adds a level for nothing. |

Classification (design-interfaces): role is config of the mapping. Owner is the user. It
changes per subscription, when the user edits it. Not a credential, not routing.

### 2. Default for new and old automations

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **`True` as the field default; absent means on** | Old rows have no key, so they read `True`. Old automations start to work. No backfill. |
| Default off, backfill on | Needs a data migration for the same result. |
| `Optional[bool] = None`, `None` means on | Three states for one switch. The frontend must treat `null` and `undefined` both as on. |

### 3. Where the event goes in the agent's inputs

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **Append to the last user message** | The runner takes the tail user message as the turn (`services/runner/src/protocol.ts:1077-1086`), so the agent reads the instruction and the event together. A string content stays a string; a list content gets one more text part. |
| A second user message after the instruction | The instruction becomes history, not the current turn. Some harnesses treat it as prior context. |
| A system message | `system` messages go to `AGENTS.md` text (`dtos.py:1715-1730`), not to the turn. The event is turn data, not standing instruction. |
| A sibling input key (`inputs.event`) | The agent handler never reads it (`handler.py:479`). This is today's broken workaround. |

The shape rules, applied to the resolved inputs:

| Resolved inputs | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `messages` list, last message has `role: "user"` | Event text appended to that message. |
| `messages` list, last message is not a user message | A new user message with the event text is appended. |
| `{}` (no mapping keys) | `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<event text>"}]}`. |
| Anything else (a completion mapping such as `{"number": 42}`, or the whole-context `"$"` mapping) | Unchanged. The `"$"` mapping already carries the event. A completion mapping names its own inputs. |

Event text (agent-facing, shown in the run transcript):

~~~text

Event data (GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_EVENT):
```json
{
  "action": "opened",
  "number": 42,
  "title": "Fix the login page"
}
```
~~~

- It starts with a blank line, because the runner joins text blocks with no separator.
- The JSON is `json.dumps(attributes, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)`.
- When `event_type` is absent, the header is `Event data:`.
- In the `{}` case the leading blank line is dropped.

### 4. Size cap on the event text

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **Cut the JSON at 20,000 characters, then add `(The event data was cut: N more characters.)`** | One large email body cannot fill the model context. 20,000 characters is about 5,000 tokens. The cut JSON is not valid JSON; the note says so. |
| No cap | A large payload costs tokens on every run and can push the instruction out of a small context. |
| Drop large fields | Needs rules per field. More code for a rare case. |

The cap is a module constant `TRIGGER_EVENT_TEXT_MAX_CHARS = 20_000` in
`api/oss/src/core/triggers/dtos.py`, next to `TRIGGER_MAX_RETRIES`.

### 5. Text coercion after resolution

The resolver replaces a whole leaf with its value, so a pill on a number gives `text: 42`, on
an object gives a dict, and on an absent key gives `None`. Pydantic rejects all three in the
agent handler (verified with a script; see the research file).

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **The dispatcher coerces each message `content` and each text part `text` to a string** | One place, before the request is built and before the delivery is written. A dict or list becomes compact JSON, a number or boolean becomes `str()`, `None` becomes `""`. |
| Coerce in the SDK handler | Fixes it for every caller, but the runner and services can run a different SDK version than the API. The API fix works at once. |
| Make the frontend refuse pills on non-string fields | The schema can be wrong, and absent keys still give `None`. |

Coercion runs whether `include_event` is on or off. It touches only the `messages` list.

### 6. Recording the event on the delivery

The preview needs real values. A delivery stores only resolved inputs.

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **`TriggerDeliveryData.event: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]` = the context's `event` block** | The selector `$.event.attributes.title` resolves against `{event: delivery.data.event}` with no change. No migration. Stores the payload once more per delivery. |
| Parse the event JSON back out of the attached text | Breaks when the option is off or when the text was cut. Couples the screen to a text format. |
| No real values in the preview | The user cannot see a schema mismatch until the agent fails. |

Set on subscription deliveries only (real runs, refusals that have the event, and test
captures). Schedules have a synthetic event; they keep `event` absent.

### 7. Where the field cards come from

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **The catalog payload schema** | Available before the first event. Carries the provider's `description`. The query exists. |
| Keys of the last delivery | Real keys, but empty until the first event, and no descriptions. |
| Both, merged | Handles a schema mismatch, but adds merge rules before we know a mismatch happens. |

Card rules:

- One card per property of `payload.properties`, in schema order.
- A property of type `object` with its own `properties` is a group: the group shows its
  humanized name and one card per child property. Deeper objects are one card each.
- An array is one card.
- Label: split camelCase into words, then `humanizeActionKey` from `@agenta/shared/utils`
  (`web/packages/agenta-shared/src/utils/toolSlug.ts:67-81`). `createdBy` reads "Created by",
  `htmlUrl` reads "Html URL". A child label is the parent and child words together:
  `data.title` reads "Data title". No hand-written label map.
- Description: the property's `description`, as the provider wrote it. No description: no line.
- Selector: `$.event.attributes.<key>`, or `$.event.attributes["<key>"]` when the key is not
  letters, digits and underscores.
- A card shows a check when the template already has its selector.
- No schema, or an empty `properties`: no cards. The checkbox and the preview still show.

### 8. Run now

Run now opens a new chat with the instruction. It has no event of its own.

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **Use the last delivery's event: fill pills with its values, and add the event text when the option is on. With no delivery, each pill becomes its label in square brackets.** | Run now sends what the preview shows. The user tests with real data when it exists. |
| Send pills as raw selectors | The agent reads `$.event.attributes.title`. Wrong. |
| Block Run now until a delivery exists | A new automation cannot be tried at all. |

The frontend builds the event text with the same format as the dispatcher. Both sides have a
test that pins the same example string.

### 9. Where the frontend code lives

| Part | Package | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| zod fields, schema-to-cards, labels, used-field check, preview text, event text | `@agenta/entities/gatewayTrigger/core` | Pure functions next to `eventMessageTemplate.ts`. Unit tests with vitest. |
| `EventMessageComposer` (pill editor), `EventFieldCards` | `@agenta/entity-ui/gatewayTrigger/drawers/subscription/` | Reusable UI next to `MessageComposer`. `PillEditor.tsx` comes back from `89c2d80c39^`. |
| Instruction field wiring, drafts, payload builders | `@agenta/automation-ui` | The feature that owns the automation screens. |
| Run now | `web/mobile/src/features/automations/` | The button is a `/m` app component today. |

### 10. Reading and writing the mapping

`parseMessageTemplate` returns `""` when the mapping has any key other than the message
(`eventMessageTemplate.ts:126-138`). A builder agent's mapping often has a sibling `event` key,
so the screen would show an empty box and Save would drop that key.

Decision: `parseMessageTemplate` reads the message and ignores other keys. A new
`writeMessageTemplate(inputsText, template, isChat, primaryKey)` replaces only the message key
and keeps the rest, the same rule `setScheduleMessage` follows (`messageInputs.ts:100-118`).
A mapping the composer cannot show (several messages, a non-user message, a non-text part)
keeps today's warning line and is replaced only when the user types.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- **The delivered keys may not match the schema.** Not verified: no real delivery is on record
  in the repo or the local databases. If a key differs, its pill gives an empty string, and the
  attached event still carries the real key. QA records one real GitHub payload and compares.
- **Old automations change behavior.** Their agents start to get the event text. That is the
  fix, but a prompt that depended on not seeing it may act differently. The user can turn the
  option off.
- **The transcript shows the event JSON.** The attached text is part of the user message, so the
  session view shows it. This is honest about what the agent got.
- **Storage.** Each subscription delivery stores the payload in `data.event`, and, when the
  option is on, a second copy inside `data.inputs`. Composio payloads are small JSON objects.
  No cap on the stored copy.
- **Typed text that starts with `$` or `/`** is read as a selector by the resolver, today and
  after this change (`resolvers.py:128-133`). Recorded as a known limit.
- **Two copies of the event text format** (Python and TypeScript). Pinned by one shared example
  in both test suites.
- **Version skew.** The SDK reference text ships with the SDK. The dispatcher change ships with
  the API. Neither depends on the other.

## Migration

- No schema migration. `data` is a JSON column on both tables.
- Old subscriptions read `include_event = True`.
- Old deliveries have no `event`. The preview falls back to field labels for them.
- Rollback: revert the API image. Rows written with `include_event` or `event` still read on
  the old code, because `TriggerSubscriptionData` and `TriggerDeliveryData` ignore unknown keys
  (Pydantic default). Check this in the backend tasks.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run one read-only Codex review with one lens, in its own detached worktree.
#
# Usage:
#   codex_review.sh <clone-dir> <out-dir> <label> <lens> <base-sha> <head-sha> [context-file]
#
#   clone-dir     plain git clone (created if missing). Never a GitButler workspace.
#   out-dir       where the report goes: <out-dir>/<label>-codex-<lens>.md (+ .log)
#   label         round label, for example r1
#   lens          simplify | slop | correctness | security | naming
#   base-sha      diff base (merge base of the PR head and its base branch);
#                 "design" in design mode
#   head-sha      PR head commit; in design mode, the commit the design applies to
#   context-file  optional file of settled decisions and owner rules
#
# Design mode: set REVIEW_DESIGN to a spec folder or a doc. The lens must be simplify or naming.
# The script puts every Markdown file of the design into the brief, so the design may be
# uncommitted, and Codex reads today's code at head-sha.
#
# Environment:
#   CODEX_MODEL   default gpt-6-astra
#   CODEX_EFFORT  default medium
#   REVIEW_REPO_URL  default https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta.git
#   REVIEW_PR     optional PR number; fetches pull/<n>/head when the head is on a fork
#   REVIEW_DESIGN optional spec folder or doc; turns on design mode
set -euo pipefail

if [ $# -lt 6 ]; then
  sed -n '2,20p' "$0" >&2
  exit 2
fi

clone=$(realpath -m "$1") outdir=$2 label=$3 lens=$4 base=$5 head=$6 context=${7:-}
model=${CODEX_MODEL:-gpt-6-astra}
effort=${CODEX_EFFORT:-medium}
repo_url=${REVIEW_REPO_URL:-https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta.git}
skills=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
lens_dir=$skills/review-$lens

case $lens in simplify|slop|correctness|security|naming) ;; *) echo "unknown lens: $lens" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
# The naming lens applies rules kept in reference files; put them into the brief.
refs=()
if [ "$lens" = naming ]; then
  refs=("$lens_dir/references/"{checks,report-template,calibration}.md
        "$skills/naming-and-resources/references/"{project-conventions,naming-rules,layer-name-table,resource-template}.md)
fi
design=${REVIEW_DESIGN:-}
if [ -n "$design" ]; then
  case $lens in simplify|naming) ;; *) echo "design mode supports the simplify and naming lenses only" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
  [ -e "$design" ] || { echo "missing design: $design" >&2; exit 2; }
  design=$(realpath "$design")
fi
[ -f "$lens_dir/lens.md" ] || { echo "missing $lens_dir/lens.md" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -z "$context" ] || [ -f "$context" ] || { echo "missing context file: $context" >&2; exit 2; }

# Refuse the GitButler workspace: its index and branches belong to someone else.
if [ "$clone" = "$(realpath -m ~/code/agenta)" ]; then

fi
if [ -d "$clone/.git" ] && [ "$(git -C "$clone" branch --show-current)" = gitbutler/workspace ]; then
  echo "refusing a GitButler workspace clone: $clone" >&2; exit 2
fi

codex=$(command -v codex || ls -1 ~/.nvm/versions/node/*/bin/codex 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$codex" ] || { echo "codex not found" >&2; exit 2; }
export PATH="$(dirname "$codex"):$PATH"

mkdir -p "$outdir"
outdir=$(realpath "$outdir")
out=$outdir/$label-codex-$lens.md
log=$outdir/$label-codex-$lens.log

# Plain clone, shared by all runs. Each run gets its own worktree, because two runs
# in one folder collide on the git index lock.
if [ ! -d "$clone/.git" ]; then
  git clone -q --filter=blob:none --no-checkout "$repo_url" "$clone"
fi
has() { git -C "$clone" cat-file -e "$1^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; }
[ -n "$design" ] && base=$head
has "$head" && has "$base" || git -C "$clone" fetch -q origin "$head" "$base" 2>/dev/null || true
if ! has "$head" && [ -n "${REVIEW_PR:-}" ]; then
  git -C "$clone" fetch -q origin "pull/$REVIEW_PR/head"
fi
has "$head" || { echo "cannot fetch head $head" >&2; exit 1; }
has "$base" || { echo "cannot fetch base $base" >&2; exit 1; }

wt=$clone.wt/$label-$lens-$$
mkdir -p "$clone.wt"
git -C "$clone" worktree add -q --detach "$wt" "$head"
brief=$(mktemp "$outdir/.brief-$label-$lens.XXXXXX")
cleanup() {
  rm -f "$brief"
  git -C "$clone" worktree remove --force "$wt" 2>/dev/null || rm -rf "$wt"
  git -C "$clone" worktree prune
}
trap cleanup EXIT

{
  awk 'n >= 2; /^---$/ && n < 2 { n++ }' "$lens_dir/SKILL.md"
  echo
  echo "## lens.md"
  echo
  cat "$lens_dir/lens.md"
  echo
  for f in "${refs[@]}"; do
    echo "## Reference: ${f#$skills/}"
    echo
    cat "$f"
    echo
  done
  echo "## Review context"
  if [ -n "$design" ]; then
    echo "Target: design."
    echo "Checkout path: $wt (today's code, detached at $head)."
    echo "Design: $design. Its files follow."
    echo "Version: $head plus the design files below."
    if [ -d "$design" ]; then files=$(find "$design" -type f -name '*.md' ! -name 'review-loop.md' | sort)
    else files=$design; fi
    for f in $files; do
      echo
      echo "### Design file: ${f#$(dirname "$design")/}"
      echo
      cat "$f"
    done
  else
    echo "Checkout path: $wt (detached at the head commit)."
    echo "Base: $base"
    echo "Head: $head"
    echo "Read the change with: git -C $wt diff $base $head   (add -- <path> per file)"
    echo "Changed files:"
    git -C "$wt" diff --stat "$base" "$head" | tail -n 200
  fi
  if [ -n "$context" ]; then
    echo
    echo "## Context file (settled decisions)"
    cat "$context"
  fi

"$codex" exec -m "$model" -c model_reasoning_effort="$effort" \
  --sandbox read-only --color never -C "$wt" -o "$out" - < "$brief" > "$log" 2>&1

echo "done: $out"
grep -E '^Rating: ' "$out" | tail -1 || echo "Rating: missing"
# Event field picker for event automations — HANDOFF

## Goal
Event automations (Composio trigger subscriptions) run the agent with only the typed instruction.
The event data never reaches the agent. Build:
1. Backend: an option on the trigger subscription ("attach the full event", on by default, on for
   existing automations). When on, the dispatcher adds the event to the agent's message.
2. Frontend (/m automation screens): field cards from the catalog event payload schema under the
   Instruction field; a click inserts a pill stored as `$.event.attributes.<key>`; a preview from
   the last delivery; the attach-full-event checkbox.

## Root cause (verified in code on origin/release/v0.127.1)
- Commit 89c2d80c39 (2026-09-08) deleted the old subscription form with the event field picker.
- Event automations use the schedule `MessageComposer`, a plain textarea storing static text.
- `compileMessageTemplate` / `parseMessageTemplate` in `@agenta/entities/gatewayTrigger` still exist, unused.
- Catalog `get_event` already returns the Composio `payload` JSON Schema; no UI reads it.

## Approved design
Mockup approved by Mahmoud 2026-10-29 ("Yes, build it"). Field cards use Composio's description.
Checkbox copy from the mockup: "Also attach the full event, so the agent can use any detail".
Labels: humanized field names (no hand-written label map, to avoid invented copy).

## Tier: Feature. Base: origin/release/v0.127.1.

## State
- [x] 1 research  - [x] 2 spec  - [ ] 3 design review  - [ ] 5 implement  - [ ] 6/7 review loops  - [ ] 8 QA  - [ ] 9 PR ready

## Block 1 and 2 outputs (2026-10-29)
- Research: ~/agenta-build-event-field-picker/research.md
- Spec (not in the repo, the main checkout is a shared GitButler workspace): ~/agenta-build-event-field-picker/spec/openspec/changes/attach-event-to-automation-runs/
  Copy it to `openspec/changes/attach-event-to-automation-runs/` in the implementation branch. Validates with `--strict`.
- Spec viewer: https://claude.ai/artifact/RVGpysyTteLBrk7PakiirT
- Field: `TriggerSubscriptionData.include_event: bool = True` (data JSON column, no migration). Delivery gets `data.event`.
- Dispatcher: coerce message text to strings, then append event text (header + fenced JSON of event.attributes, cap 20,000 chars) to the last user message; `{}` becomes one user message; other shapes unchanged.
- New finding: a pill on a number/object/absent field fails the run (pydantic rejects non-str text). Evidence: evidence/check_text_coercion.*
- New finding: the builder-agent reference recommends a sibling `event` input key that the agent handler never reads.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Field cards for event automations

For an event automation, the Instruction field SHALL show a grid of field cards under the instruction box, built from the catalog payload schema of the automation's event. Schedules SHALL keep today's composer.

#### Scenario: Flat schema

- **WHEN** the event is the GitHub pull request event, whose schema has `action`, `createdAt`, `createdBy`, `description`, `number`, `title` and `url`
- **THEN** seven cards show, in schema order, each with its humanized name and the schema's `description`

#### Scenario: Nested object

- **WHEN** a property is an object with its own `properties`, such as Linear's `data`
- **THEN** the object shows as a group named for it, with one card per child property, and deeper objects show as one card each

#### Scenario: No schema

- **WHEN** the catalog returns no payload schema, or the query fails
- **THEN** no cards show and the instruction box, the checkbox and the preview still work

### Requirement: Card labels come from the key

A card label SHALL be the property key split at camelCase and underscores, in sentence case, with known acronyms in capitals, through `humanizeActionKey`. A child label SHALL join the parent and child words. No hand-written label map SHALL exist.

#### Scenario: camelCase key

- **WHEN** the key is `createdBy`
- **THEN** the label is "Created by"

#### Scenario: Acronym

- **WHEN** the key is `url`
- **THEN** the label is "URL"

### Requirement: Pills

A click on a card SHALL insert a pill for that field at the cursor. The pill SHALL show the card label. The mapping SHALL store the field as the selector `$.event.attributes.<key>`. A pill SHALL be removable like one character.

#### Scenario: Insert

- **WHEN** the user types "Review " and clicks the "Title" card
- **THEN** the box shows "Review " and a "Title" pill, and the stored content is `[{"type":"text","text":"Review "},{"type":"text","text":"$.event.attributes.title"}]`

#### Scenario: Used card

- **WHEN** the instruction already has a "Title" pill
- **THEN** the "Title" card shows a check

#### Scenario: Remove

- **WHEN** the user deletes the pill with Backspace
- **THEN** the selector leaves the stored content and the card loses its check

#### Scenario: Key with special characters

- **WHEN** a key has a character other than letters, digits and underscores
- **THEN** the selector uses bracket form, `$.event.attributes["<key>"]`

### Requirement: Other mapping keys are kept

Reading and writing the instruction SHALL change only the message key of the mapping and SHALL keep every other key.

#### Scenario: Agent-made mapping

- **WHEN** a stored mapping is `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Triage it"}],"event":"$.event.attributes"}` and the user edits the text
- **THEN** the saved mapping still has the `event` key

### Requirement: Attach-full-event checkbox

The Instruction field SHALL show a checkbox labeled "Also attach the full event, so the agent can use any detail" for event automations. It SHALL read `data.include_event`, treat an absent value as checked, and save its value with the rest of the draft.

#### Scenario: Existing automation

- **WHEN** an automation saved before this change opens
- **THEN** the checkbox is checked

#### Scenario: New automation

- **WHEN** the user creates an event automation and does not touch the checkbox
- **THEN** the create payload has `data.include_event` equal to `true`

#### Scenario: Unsaved change

- **WHEN** the user unchecks it on the detail screen
- **THEN** the save bar shows, and Discard checks it again

### Requirement: What the agent gets preview

The Instruction field SHALL show a "What the agent gets" preview of the message. Pills SHALL show values from `data.event` of the newest delivery that has one, else their labels. When the checkbox is on, the preview SHALL show that the full event is added, with its JSON when a delivery has one.

#### Scenario: With a delivery

- **WHEN** the newest delivery with `data.event` has `attributes.title` equal to "Fix the login page"
- **THEN** the "Title" pill reads "Fix the login page" in the preview

#### Scenario: Without a delivery

- **WHEN** no delivery has `data.event`
- **THEN** the pills show their labels and the preview states that the full event is added when one arrives

### Requirement: Run now uses the same message

Run now SHALL send the text the preview shows: pills filled from the newest delivery with `data.event`, each pill as its label in square brackets when there is none, and the event text added when the checkbox is saved as on and an event exists.

#### Scenario: Run now with a delivery

- **WHEN** the user presses Run now and a delivery with `data.event` exists
- **THEN** the new chat's first message has the filled values and, when the option is on, the event text in the dispatcher's format

#### Scenario: Run now with pills and no delivery

- **WHEN** no delivery exists
- **THEN** the first message has "[Title]" where the "Title" pill is
## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Include-event option on subscriptions

A trigger subscription SHALL carry `data.include_event`, a boolean that defaults to true. A stored subscription without the key SHALL read as true.

#### Scenario: Old subscription reads as on

- **WHEN** a subscription row was saved before this change and its `data` has no `include_event` key
- **THEN** the API returns it with `data.include_event` equal to `true`

#### Scenario: The user turns it off

- **WHEN** a client edits a subscription with `data.include_event` set to `false`
- **THEN** the stored row keeps `false` and later reads return `false`

#### Scenario: No migration

- **WHEN** the change is deployed
- **THEN** no database migration runs, because `data` is a JSON column

### Requirement: Event attached to the agent's message

When `include_event` is true and the event has attributes, the dispatcher SHALL add the event text to the resolved inputs before it sends them. The event text is a blank line, a header that names the event type, and the JSON of `event.attributes` in a fenced block.

#### Scenario: Chat mapping with a string instruction

- **WHEN** the resolved inputs are `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Review this pull request"}]}`
- **THEN** the sent content is `"Review this pull request"` followed by the event text, as one string

#### Scenario: Chat mapping with text parts

- **WHEN** the last user message has a list of text parts
- **THEN** one more text part with the event text is appended to that list

#### Scenario: Last message is not a user message

- **WHEN** the resolved `messages` list ends with a message whose role is not `user`
- **THEN** a new user message with the event text is appended

#### Scenario: Empty mapping

- **WHEN** the mapping is `{}`
- **THEN** the inputs become one user message whose content is the event text without the leading blank line

#### Scenario: Other mapping shapes stay unchanged

- **WHEN** the resolved inputs have no `messages` list and are not empty, for example `{"number": 42}` or the whole context from a `"$"` mapping
- **THEN** the inputs are sent unchanged

#### Scenario: Option off

- **WHEN** `include_event` is false
- **THEN** no event text is added

#### Scenario: Event without attributes

- **WHEN** the event's `attributes` is absent or null
- **THEN** no event text is added

### Requirement: Event text size cap

The JSON in the event text SHALL be cut at `TRIGGER_EVENT_TEXT_MAX_CHARS` (20,000) characters, followed by a line that states how many characters were cut.

#### Scenario: Large payload

- **WHEN** the JSON of `event.attributes` is 25,000 characters long
- **THEN** the event text holds the first 20,000 characters and the line `(The event data was cut: 5000 more characters.)`

### Requirement: Message text is always a string

After it resolves the mapping, the dispatcher SHALL turn each `content` value of a message in `messages`, and each `text` value of a text part in such a content list, into a string, whether or not `include_event` is on.

#### Scenario: Number field

- **WHEN** a text part's selector resolves to the integer `42`
- **THEN** the sent part is `{"type":"text","text":"42"}`

#### Scenario: Object field

- **WHEN** a selector resolves to an object
- **THEN** the sent text is the compact JSON of that object

#### Scenario: Absent field

- **WHEN** a selector resolves to nothing
- **THEN** the sent text is the empty string and the run does not fail

### Requirement: Delivery records the event

Each subscription delivery that the dispatcher writes with a resolved event SHALL store the event context block (`event_id`, `event_type`, `timestamp`, `created_at`, `attributes`) in `data.event`. Schedule deliveries SHALL NOT set it.

#### Scenario: Successful run

- **WHEN** an event runs the agent
- **THEN** the delivery's `data.event.attributes` equals the provider payload and `data.inputs` equals the inputs sent, event text included

#### Scenario: Schedule tick

- **WHEN** a schedule fires
- **THEN** its delivery has no `data.event`

### Requirement: Test captures match real runs

A test-mode capture SHALL build its inputs with the same coercion and event attachment as a real run, and SHALL record `data.event`.

#### Scenario: Test capture with the option on

- **WHEN** a subscription with `flags.is_test` true and `include_event` true receives an event
- **THEN** the test delivery's `data.inputs` holds the event text and `data.event` holds the event

### Requirement: Builder agent guidance

The agent-facing reference on trigger inputs SHALL state that the event is attached to the message by default and SHALL NOT recommend a sibling `event` input key.

#### Scenario: Reference text

- **WHEN** a builder agent reads the trigger inputs reference
- **THEN** it reads that `include_event` defaults to on and that the agent reads only `messages`

content.content:
# Naming review

Base: design
Head: /home/mahmoud/agenta-build-event-field-picker/spec/openspec/changes/attach-event-to-automation-runs/ at 2026-10-29, checked against d2651bc1d96924d80e842c636feac54f5ce18a3d (release/v0.127.1)

## Findings

### 1. "event" means three things on the dispatch path, and the new parameter invites the wrong one
- Category: Design finding
- Severity: Medium
- Rule: one word, one meaning inside one context (naming-rules.md 1 and 2), must; misleading name when a caller acts on it (naming-rules.md 4), must
- Where: design.md decision 3 and decision 6; tasks.md 2.1 and 3.1; `api/oss/src/tasks/asyncio/triggers/dispatcher.py:258-264`, `:93-118`, `:311-317`
- Evidence:
  - In `dispatcher.py`, the local `event` in `dispatch_subscription` (`:126`) and in `_run` (`:264`) is the raw Composio body. `_build_context` reads `event.get("metadata")` and `event.get("payload")` from it (`:100-108`).
  - `context["event"]` is the normalized block `{event_id, event_type, timestamp, created_at, attributes}` (`:110-113`).
  - The design adds `compose_event_inputs(inputs, *, event, include_event)` (tasks 2.1) and `TriggerDeliveryData.event` (decision 6). Both mean the normalized block.
  - `include_event` and the "event text" carry only `event.attributes` plus the type in the header (decision 3), not the block that `data.event` stores.
- What is wrong: The call site for `compose_event_inputs` is `_run`, where a variable named `event` already holds the raw body. The natural call `compose_event_inputs(inputs, event=event, ...)` passes the raw body. The raw body has `payload`, not `attributes`, so the rule "event without attributes: no event text" (spec `trigger-event-inputs`, scenario "Event without attributes") makes the run silently send no event. The unit tests in tasks 2.3 call the function directly with a normalized block, so they would not catch it. A reader of `include_event` next to `data.event` also guesses that the option attaches `data.event`; it attaches only `attributes`.
- Smallest fix: Rename the new parameter so it cannot take the raw body. Either pass the whole context, `compose_event_inputs(inputs, *, context, include_event)`, and read `context["event"]` inside, or name it `event_context`. State in decision 3 that the event text is built from `event.attributes` and `event.event_type`. Keep `TriggerDeliveryData.event` (the selector `$.event.attributes...` needs that key), and say in decision 6 that it holds the context block, not the provider body.

### 2. "event message" and "event text" name two different things in one package
- Category: Design finding
- Severity: Low
- Rule: confusable names for two concepts (naming-rules.md 1 and 9), should
- Where: tasks.md 7.3, 8.2, 10.1; design.md decision 9; `web/packages/agenta-entities/src/gatewayTrigger/core/eventMessageTemplate.ts:1-12`

- Category: Design finding

# Simplify review

Base: design
Head: /home/mahmoud/agenta-build-event-field-picker/spec/openspec/changes/attach-event-to-automation-runs at d2651bc1d96924d80e842c636feac54f5ce18a3d, with the supplied design files

## Findings

### 1. Run now promotes a best-effort preview into a second input composer

- Severity: Medium
- Where: `design.md`, decisions 5 and 8; `tasks.md`, sections 7.3 and 10.1; `web/packages/agenta-entities/src/gatewayTrigger/core/selectorPreview.ts:12`
- What is wrong: The proposed helpers already disagree with real dispatch. `previewValue(null)` produces `"null"`, while the proposed backend produces `""`. Booleans become `"true"` in JavaScript and `"True"` with Python `str()`. The preview resolver also splits `["a.b"]` into two path steps, although the design explicitly supports keys with special characters. Run now would execute these differences. Pinning one event-format example does not cover them.
- Smallest fix: Keep Run now, but define one bounded rendering contract for the field selectors the cards generate. Preserve quoted property keys during lookup. Use the same text rule on both sides: strings unchanged, missing/null values empty, other JSON values serialized as JSON. Share expected-value fixtures for these cases. Do not extend the frontend into a general JSONPath engine; keep unsupported mappings outside this execution contract.

### 2. Defer schedule coercion

- Severity: Low
- Where: `tasks.md`, section 3.1; `design.md`, Non-Goals and decision 5
- What is wrong: The task changes schedule inputs through coercion, although schedules are explicitly outside this feature. That adds behavior and validation work without supporting the event-field outcome.
- Smallest fix: Suggestion (non-blocking): call the new composition function only for subscriptions. Leave schedule inputs unchanged. Add schedule coercion separately if a concrete schedule use case requires it.

## What to keep

1. **Delivery event field — keep.** The approved preview needs raw values when attachment is off or the attached text is cut. A delivery snapshot avoids parsing agent-facing text or adding another store.

2. **Run now enrichment — keep with finding 1 resolved.** Reuse one frontend renderer for the preview and both Run now entry points. Sending raw selectors would make the existing action misleading.

3. **Text coercion — keep for subscriptions.** Numeric and object fields need conversion at the message boundary. Preserve content lists and non-text parts. One detail in the rationale needs correction: `ContentBlock.text` permits `None`; it does not reject all three listed cases.

4. **20,000-character cap — keep.** One constant and one cut rule are simpler than field-specific limits. Describe it as a limit on appended event text, not on the whole input: selected fields can still carry large values.

5. **PillEditor and separate event components — keep.** The existing `MessageComposer` is a small schedule textarea. Cursor handling and atomic pills are a distinct responsibility. Extending it would introduce event-specific modes into schedule editing. Keep the draft owned by the parent.

6. **Builder-agent reference update — keep in this change.** The current reference explicitly recommends the unread sibling `event` key. Correcting it removes a source of new broken mappings.

This review used the supplied design and the checkout at the stated commit. No files changed. No tests, builds, or linters ran.

### 4. Size cap on the event text

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **Cut the JSON at 20,000 characters, then add `(The event data was cut: N more characters.)`** | One large email body cannot fill the model context. 20,000 characters is about 5,000 tokens. The cut JSON is not valid JSON; the note says so. |

### 5. Text coercion after resolution

The resolver replaces a whole leaf with its value, so a pill on a number gives `text: 42`, on
an object gives a dict, and on an absent key gives `None`. Pydantic rejects all three in the
agent handler (verified with a script; see the research file).

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **The dispatcher coerces each message `content` and each text part `text` to a string** | One place, before the request is built and before the delivery is written. A dict or list becomes compact JSON, a number or boolean becomes `str()`, `None` becomes `""`. |
| Coerce in the SDK handler | Fixes it for every caller, but the runner and services can run a different SDK version than the API. The API fix works at once. |
| Make the frontend refuse pills on non-string fields | The schema can be wrong, and absent keys still give `None`. |

## Part A: Backend

### 1. DTOs (no migration)

- [ ] 1.1 Add `include_event: bool = True` to `TriggerSubscriptionData` in
  `api/oss/src/core/triggers/dtos.py`, after `inputs_fields`, with a one-line comment: adds the
  event data to the agent's message.
- [ ] 1.2 Add `event: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None` to `TriggerDeliveryData`, after `inputs`.
- [ ] 1.3 Add `TRIGGER_EVENT_TEXT_MAX_CHARS = 20_000` to the configuration block of `dtos.py`.
- [ ] 1.4 Unit test: a row dict without `include_event` validates to `True`; a dict with
  `false` round-trips through `map_subscription_dto_to_dbe_edit` and
  `map_subscription_dbe_to_dto` as `False`.
- [ ] 1.5 Unit test: the old models (without the new fields) still validate a row that has them
  (rollback safety; Pydantic ignores extra keys by default).

### 2. Inputs composition (pure function)

- [ ] 2.1 In `api/oss/src/core/triggers/utils.py`, add
  `compose_event_inputs(inputs, *, event, include_event) -> Dict[str, Any]`. It coerces message
  text (design decision 5) and attaches the event text (design decisions 3 and 4). It does not
  mutate its argument.
- [ ] 2.2 Add `format_event_text(event_type, attributes) -> str` in the same file, used by 2.1.
- [ ] 2.3 Unit tests in `api/oss/tests/pytest/unit/triggers/test_triggers_event_inputs.py`, one
  per scenario of `specs/trigger-event-inputs/spec.md`: string content, parts content, last
  message not user, `{}`, completion mapping, whole context, option off, no attributes, the
  25,000-character cut, number, object, absent value. One test pins the exact text of the
  shared example in `design.md` decision 3.

### 3. Dispatcher

- [ ] 3.1 In `_run` (`api/oss/src/tasks/asyncio/triggers/dispatcher.py:311-348`), for a
  subscription, call `compose_event_inputs` on the resolved inputs, then use the result for both
  `delivery_data.inputs` and the request. Set `delivery_data.event = context["event"]`.
  Schedules keep today's inputs (coercion only) and no `event`.
- [ ] 3.2 In the test-mode branch (`dispatcher.py:156-188`), do the same, so the test delivery
  has the composed inputs and `event`.
- [ ] 3.3 Keep `data.event` on the failed-build delivery (`dispatcher.py:433-443`): set it as
  soon as the context is built, before the mapping resolves, so a failed run still shows the
  event.
- [ ] 3.4 Update `api/oss/tests/pytest/unit/triggers/test_triggers_dispatcher.py`: the happy path
  with a `messages` mapping gets the event text; the existing `{"number": ...}` tests stay
  unchanged; a schedule run has no `event`; the test capture has `event`.

### 4. Builder agent guidance

- [ ] 4.1 In `_TRIGGER_INPUTS_REFERENCE`
  (`sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/adapters/agenta_builtins.py:518-650`), replace the sibling
  `"event": "$.event.attributes"` advice with: the agent reads only `messages`; the event is
  attached to the last user message by default (`include_event`); set `include_event: false` to
  send the instruction alone; to put one field inside the text, use text parts with a selector
  calls `humanizeActionKey`.
- [ ] 7.2 `eventMessageTemplate.ts`: `parseMessageTemplate` ignores keys other than the message
  key; add `writeMessageTemplate` that replaces only the message key; add
  `templateSelectors(template)` for the used-card check.
- [ ] 7.3 `eventPreview.ts`: `renderEventMessage(template, event, labels)` fills pills from
  `{event}` with `resolveSelectorPreview` and `previewValue`, else `[Label]`;
  `formatEventText(eventType, attributes)` mirrors the backend format and cap.
- [ ] 7.4 Export the new functions from `web/packages/agenta-entities/src/gatewayTrigger/index.ts`.
- [ ] 7.5 Vitest tests in `web/packages/agenta-entities/tests/unit/`: the GitHub pull request
  schema gives seven cards with the right labels; a Linear-style nested `data` gives a group;
  bracket selectors; sibling keys kept on write; preview with and without an event; the shared
  example string from `design.md` decision 3 is equal to `formatEventText` output.

### 8. Components in `@agenta/entity-ui/gatewayTrigger` (parallel with 7)

- [ ] 8.1 Restore `PillEditor.tsx` from `git show 89c2d80c39^:web/packages/agenta-entity-ui/src/gatewayTrigger/drawers/subscription/PillEditor.tsx`
  and adapt it: pills show `fieldLabel`, not the raw path.
